q: How do I work out the carbon footprint of a 3D printed part?
title: 3D printed part: carbon footprint
short: Add two things: the printer's electricity for that part and the material used. Electricity is the printer's average power times print hours, times 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25. Material is the filament or powder weight, including supports and failed prints, times a named factor for that polymer or metal.
audience: Prototype shops, tool rooms and product designers

p: Read the kWh from a plug meter over a few prints rather than the label rating. Powder bed and metal printers also use energy for heating and inert gas.

ul: Weigh the part and supports, or take grams from the slicer.
Add the share of failed or scrapped prints.
Use a factor for the exact material, such as PLA, ABS, nylon powder or steel powder.

senseible: Senseible reads the energy invoices behind the making stage into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, and keeps material invoices on the Scope 3 trail. Material factors come from your supplier or a named database and are labelled with their source, so the product figure can be traced line by line.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard

example.title: Example (illustrative)
lines: Printer draws 0.2 kW for 5 hours: 1.0 kWh × 0.710 = 0.71 kg CO2
Material: add grams used × your polymer factor
example.note: Illustrative quantities; use your own meter reading and material factor.
